name: Email & SMS Threat Triage
description: 1,200 synthetic emails and SMS messages, 400 each labeled legitimate, spam or phishing, with hard cases such as genuine security alerts, urgent-but-harmless spam and calm, well-written phishing.
task: How should this incoming message be classified?

labels.name: legitimate
labels.description: A normal message the recipient would expect: personal or work conversation, or transactional/account mail from a service they use (order and shipping updates, receipts, bookings, reminders, bills, password resets or one-time codes they requested, newsletters they subscribed to). Security and billing notices are legitimate when they only inform, or tell the user to open the official app or website themselves, and never ask for passwords, card details or codes or push an unrequested login link. Expected transactional mail stays legitimate even if it contains a link or a promotion.

labels.name: spam
labels.description: Unsolicited bulk or scam messaging from a sender the recipient has no relationship with: hype marketing, prize/lottery/inheritance claims, get-rich-quick and fake job offers, crypto, casino, dating, diet-pill or SEO pitches. It may be urgent and may ask the user to reply, call, buy or visit a promo site, but it does not pose as a service, institution or person the recipient already trusts and does not try to obtain login credentials, card/bank details or verification codes. If it does both of those things, it is phishing.

labels.name: phishing
labels.description: Impersonates a trusted entity (the user's bank, payment app, courier, online store, streaming, cloud or social account, crypto exchange, employer IT/HR, a manager, a known vendor, a tax or toll agency) in order to steal credentials, card or bank details, recovery phrases or one-time codes, collect a fake fee, redirect a payment or gift-card purchase, or get the user to sign in or 'verify' through a link or attachment. Typical cues are lookalike domains and unrequested account threats or deadlines, but a calm, well-written message with one of these goals is still phishing.
